native_language_semantic_policy: Statistical scientific R S3 source record, not identical Python frozen dataclass. case_evidence.description: Frozen Python 1.2 multivariate_surrogates.py public signature with explicit two-or-more dimensions and reference channel, independent NumPy PCG64 surrogate initial permutations, finite common time grid and nonconstant selected channels. Source mode accepts only original source parameters; native-only fixed permutation and Fourier phase replay rejected; legacy R extension remains unchanged.

Complete 23-/32-time 3-channel broadband common-grid curves with even/odd rFFT, nonconstant channel marginals, two independently randomized surrogates under seeds 17 and 89, nonlinear 96-point three-channel source with Rosenstein LLE, full three-way alternatives and source physical time-unit parameters. No imputation or silently altered null.

Direct typed frozen Python 1.2 public generator numerical comparison over even/odd 23-/32-time, reordered three-channel source curves and PCG64 seeds 17,89; all surrogate curves, original marginal ranks, convergence iterations and separate spectral/cross-spectral relative errors. Existing fixed NumPy permutation replay and phase-ambiguity diagnostics retained and tested separately, not treated as public Python APIs.

Reject invalid strict boolean flag, ambiguous selected reference, duplicate/missing channels, nonfinite/constant data, malformed FFT convergence controls, nonconvergent iteration with clear failed surrogate identity, and native-only fixed permutations/phase replay. Native R does not inherit Python exception types or arbitrary Python dynamic coercions.

Exact fourteen ordered source scientific surrogate result fields and original source provenance without R-only replay and RNG audit flags, or seven ordered nonlinearity result fields with complete source nested surrogate and exact ten-field null-test provenance. R S3 arrays and structures replace Python scientific frozen dataclasses.

Reference-anchored multivariate iterative amplitude-adjusted Fourier transform null surrogates with exact per-channel empirical rank distributions and approximate auto/cross-spectrum constraints, explicit error diagnostics; Rosenstein largest Lyapunov statistic compared with surrogate null using plus-one one-/two-sided Monte Carlo tail p-values. Rejection is not proof of deterministic chaos.

independent_review_status: Provisional source-scientific author review only; no independent scientific certification and no exact-head CI pass.
language_specific_limits: R S3 native scientific records are not Python frozen dataclasses and native R exceptions do not inherit Python exception classes.

NumPy random_state=NULL obtains entropy and differs in realized draws from native ambient R RNG, while the stochastic surrogate null remains defined; deterministic NumPy PCG64 seed paths are source compared.
Near-zero target Fourier phases create machine-precision sensitivity; such unresolved bins are audited but source public API does not expose fixed replay for equivalence claims.
Exact per-channel empirical marginal distributions and approximate auto/cross-spectral fit are the scientific properties, not a guarantee of bitwise FFT identity across NumPy and base R.
Explicit native fixed initial permutations and Fourier-phase replay are out-of-source extensions and are rejected in strict source mode.
